claim: Exact sparse named-field memory needs at least log2 choose(n,k)+kb bits under distinguishability and no external memory.
limitation: Not a novel theorem; hindsight relevance does not imply online identifiability.

claim: Sequential memory must respect when X, S, and J become available.
limitation: The finite model explicitly leaves S and J public at their specified stages.

claim: The isolated first and second cut errors in the four-bit example are 3/16 and 1/4.
limitation: Uniform independent source and specified query distributions only.

claim: Attaining the child-optimal 1/4 error requires at least eight parent states and three bits suffice.
limitation: Checked restricted example; no novelty certification or general scaling result.

claim: The two-bit-then-one-bit chain has error at least 49/192.
limitation: Historical conservative bound from the September 18 certificate; superseded in strength by the September 19 exact computation C21.

claim: The record diagnostic has 810 configurations and favors sound retirement over plain LRU in its constructed setting.
limitation: No LLMs; explicit retirement signals; configurations are not independent benchmark samples.

claim: Visible history edits can also alter provider-managed reasoning state.
limitation: Model and API specific; recheck current continuity requirements before experiments.

claim: Shorter prompts do not by themselves establish lower total-run cost.
limitation: Cache behavior, future reuse, manager calls, retrieval, and retries affect the result.

claim: Native compaction, structured retention, and compatible masking are necessary comparison candidates.
limitation: Their relative performance has not been evaluated by this project.

claim: A novel structural compatibility result or a reproducible practical improvement would be the candidate contribution.
limitation: The scaling derivation is locally audited; external review and novelty comparison remain open. No production gains have been established.

claim: In the independent four-bit block family with a late block and omission reveal and one child bit, attaining error 1/4 requires exactly 3k parent bits; 2k bits suffice for the isolated first cut to attain error 3/16.
limitation: Specific independent source and public-side-information timing. Arbitrary joint encoders allowed. External review and novelty comparison outstanding.

claim: In that block family, any 2k-bit-parent then one-bit-child chain has error strictly greater than 1/4 + 1/512 for every k >= 1.
limitation: Conservative analytic lower bound with an analytic entropy lemma and independent finite checks, not an exact optimum or LLM effect. External review and novelty comparison outstanding.

claim: In the even-n (n >= 4) leave-one-out family, exact child-optimal error needs at least ceil(log2(2n)) parent bits, but a one-bit chain has excess error O(n^(-3/2)).
limitation: A separate family from C11-C12; growing exact memory does not imply a nonvanishing excess-error gap. Novelty unresolved.

claim: The artifact/manifest environment implements two forced record-memory boundaries, costed early inspection, revisions, a delayed terminal verifier, and paired restoration; 320 scripted development configurations are reproducible.
limitation: Trusted scripted policies, synthetic costs, record slots rather than information bits. Not independent LLM trials, a new optimal policy, or a native-harness comparison.

claim: In the 16 tight/cheap development cases, structured retention succeeds 16/16 with early inspection versus 9/16 without it at mean costs 11 versus 10 synthetic units; ample initial memory removes the need to inspect.
limitation: Fixed constructed cases demonstrate the intended mechanism; no sampling significance, real-world prevalence, or API cost claim.

claim: For fixed optimal branch functions, the exact-target confusability graph is complete multipartite with parts equal to joint-signature fibers.
limitation: A reformulation of the existing signature argument; general graph-based functional compression is established prior work.

claim: For the declared uniform-route atomic-record model with reliable recovery and nonbinding episode limits, the convex hull of four endpoint strategies gives the exact success versus expected incremental-cost frontier.
limitation: Restricted record selection and randomized policies completing the workflow. Not arbitrary bit coding, a hard spending-budget optimum, or a new general value-of-information theorem.

claim: For six jobs and two candidate/record slots without revisions, exact uninspected hit probability is 1/3 and inspected hit probability is one; at inspection price one the success-one recovery break-even price is 3/2.
limitation: Synthetic access cost with reliable recovery. Archive storage costs and API dollars are outside the model.

claim: Under the known first-candidate revision rule in that case, optimal uninspected hit probability rises to 4/5 and the recovery break-even price rises to five.
limitation: Depends on the lexicographic revision schedule and public routing distribution; not a general claim about revisions.

claim: With one child record in the no-revision six-job case, inspection raises hit probability from 3/10 to 1/2 but raises success-one expected extra cost from 14/5 to three when inspection costs one and recovery four.
limitation: A constructed negative economic control: improved retention need not mean lower full-run cost. No LLM outcome.

claim: The uniform four-bit two-bit-parent/one-bit-child chain has exact minimum error 9/32, attained by 128 of the 171798901 four-cell parent partitions.
limitation: Finite uniform-source/subset/query model with public omission/query at the stated stages. Locally checked computational optimum; no novelty or LLM claim. Does not establish the same gap for jointly encoded multiple blocks.

claim: The offline pilot plan specifies six calibrated regimes with 12 decision requests and 180 paired episodes under a 432-request maximum.
limitation: Historical full-schedule counts; only the separately frozen 96-request development tranche has run (C25). Held-out renderers and launch remain unfinished. Family/route effects are confounded; two strict population preferences become sampled fixed-policy ties. Not a powered benchmark.

claim: With reliable recovery and exact scripted submission in pilot Stage B, empty retention still permits successful completion; success alone does not measure retention quality.
limitation: Control covers all 30 routes in six regimes with unchanged capacities and no model calls. Schema/execution failures remain possible. Pre-recovery availability and full cost are the behavioral outcomes in this restricted design.

claim: The development request interface and runner pass fake-client controls with deleted-data and evaluator-label exclusion; optimal and forget-all controls each complete 36 episodes in 96 fake requests.
limitation: Trusted Python fake-client checks only; these controls make zero model requests. Provider transport and the later live result are separate evidence (C25). One development route; no general superiority or held-out result.

claim: The frozen Luna development tranche completed 96 valid requests: 10/12 exact-reference inspection choices and 36 completed workflow episodes with pre-recovery evidence in 21/36 and 15 recoveries.
limitation: Mutable gpt-5.6-luna alias at low effort through a controlled subscription adapter. One repeated development route; no held-out calls or native-harness comparison. Reliable recovery makes success insufficient evidence of retention. Conservative usage 2.5395 credit equivalents is not observed billing. Fixed-route policy cost differences and tie-breaking do not establish population superiority; inaccessible server internals unverified.

claim: Exact post-hoc grading of the 36 saved Luna parent selections finds three strict deficits, all in uninspected revision conditions; all 36 observed child selections are optimal conditional on their available records.
limitation: Zero new model calls. Seventeen uninspected parent choices use all 30 uniform routes; nineteen inspected choices condition on their visible manifest and two targets. Parent grading assumes an optimal child, not unobserved counterfactual Luna behavior. Other 33 parents attain their same-view reference. Does not identify internal reasoning or establish total model-policy regret.

claim: A separate 24-request development diagnostic is specified to compare first-candidate refresh, last-candidate refresh, and no refresh under counterbalanced visible-record orders.
limitation: Prepared offline only; five fake controls make 120 fake calls and zero model calls. Each future response is graded over 30 routes with a guaranteed optimal child; those routes are not model trials. New allocation is pending after the initial 96-request tranche. Canonical metadata/schema order remains an ordering channel. No held-out or generalization result.
